posts.title: Latest reported figures: 1,290 confirmed dead
body: These figures are read automatically from the published reports as they appear, and are not written or checked by hand. confirmed dead: 1,290, up from 1,259, reported by Nepalnews.
Where a report describes one district or one stretch of river rather than the national figure, it is not used here. Out of contact does not mean dead.

posts.title: Missing flood victims’ families called for DNA testing
body: September 3, Kathmandu Nepal Police has begun a DNA testing process to search for citizens who went missing in the Bhotekoshi River flood in Rasuwa, and to identify unclaimed bodies and human remains that have been recovered.
Reported by Onlinekhabar. Read automatically from that report; follow the link for the full story.

posts.title: Nepal Police put the Nepal count at 768 at 2pm Sunday
body: Nepal Police bulletin 10275 said the number of bodies found in Nepal had reached 768 by 2pm Sunday, the figure at that hour. Its district count was Chitwan 264, Nawalparasi East 194, Nawalparasi West 100, Gorkha 58, Nuwakot 52, Dhading 50, Tanahun 37 and Rasuwa 13, which added exactly to that figure.

NDRRMA's 1pm Sunday situation update remains the latest confirmed report for the other totals: 2,502 people out of contact and 8,730 rescued, Onlinekhabar reports. It does not publish a current agency or location breakdown for the rescue total, so none is inferred.

The police bulletin changes the Nepal death total from 752 at 1pm to 768 at 2pm. Out of contact does not mean dead. Families should use official police and local authority channels, not unverified social media posts.

posts.title: China sends 50 tonnes of emergency supplies to Nepal
body: China sent 50 tonnes of emergency relief supplies to Nepal on Sunday, The Kathmandu Post reports. Two Chinese military transport aircraft carried 13,200 items to Kathmandu at around 7am.

The Kathmandu Post says the supplies include tents, blankets, sleeping bags, hard tack and first-aid kits. The Chinese Embassy also said five tunnel experts had flown to flood-hit areas and four more would be sent soon.
Relief delivery is separate from the search for people trapped in hydropower tunnels. Coordinate aid through district relief committees or response agencies.

posts.title: Fresh flood warning issued as Bhotekoshi rises
body: Authorities in Nepal warned of possible fresh flooding on Sunday after water levels rose in the Bhotekoshi River, the Associated Press reports. Warning notices reached people's phones through Sunday morning.

The Associated Press says Dharam Raj Uprety, chief executive of NDRRMA, told it that Chinese authorities had reported increased water flow upstream. Residents in flood-hit districts were urged to remain on high alert.
Rescue crews were clearing the Prithvi Highway while residents in Galchhi moved to higher ground. Stay away from riverbanks and follow local warnings.

posts.title: Foreign tunnel-rescue teams now working in flood zone
body: The Kathmandu Post reports that Indian, Chinese and South Korean teams reached flood-hit areas Saturday to support specialised tunnel rescue. The 11-member Indian reconnaissance team flew to Chilime and Langtang with Nepali Army and Armed Police Force personnel.
China's Ministry of Emergency Management sent five tunnel experts to Nepal, and the Chinese Embassy said another four would be sent soon, The Kathmandu Post reports.

South Korean experts were also allowed to inspect affected areas. This is specialised assistance for tunnel rescue, forensic and DNA work, not a broad foreign deployment. People searching for relatives should use official control rooms and police channels.

posts.title: PM says more than Rs 5bn deposited for flood relief
body: Prime Minister Balen Shah said Rs 5.04 billion has been deposited in nine commercial bank accounts for flood rescue and relief, Onlinekhabar reports.

The same report says another US$1.8 million has been deposited at Himalayan Bank and Laxmi Bank. The government urges donors to use only its published QR code and bank accounts because fake collection links are circulating.

posts.title: Experts say immediate lake-burst risk has fallen, caution remains
body: The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology says the immediate risk of a sudden lake burst has fallen after water began flowing out naturally, Onlinekhabar reports.
Experts warn that fresh landslides could still trigger renewed flooding. This is a change from earlier reports that described the water body as a possible immediate threat.
Stay away from the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli riverbanks until local officials say it is safe.

posts.title: IPPAN says 898 people remain missing at hydropower sites
body: The Independent Power Producers’ Association, Nepal says 898 people remain unaccounted for at 11 hydropower projects in Rasuwa and Nuwakot, Onlinekhabar reports.
The association says 361 people have been evacuated, including 254 from Upper Trishuli-1, and around 300 are believed trapped inside that project's tunnel.
This is a project-site count with a different scope from Nepal Police's wider missing list. Chinese experts have arrived to help with tunnel rescue, Onlinekhabar reports.

posts.title: Tourism Board says 187 tourists rescued or accounted for
body: The Nepal Tourism Board's latest update says 184 foreign tourists have been rescued from flood-affected areas and three others have come back into contact, Onlinekhabar reports.
That puts 187 tourists rescued or accounted for. The board says 420 tourists remain out of contact, a separate count from NDRRMA's wider list of 2,426 people in Nepal.
Out of contact does not mean dead. Families looking for someone should use the Foreign Ministry's emergency control room and local police rather than rely on unverified social media posts.

posts.title: Ministry says power is back in five Nuwakot areas as repairs continue
body: The Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation says electricity has been restored in Kharanitar, Samundratar, Chaugada, Likhu and Panchkanya in Nuwakot by pulling lines from Sindhupalchok, Nepal News reports.

The ministry also says power is back in Gajuri, Malekhu and Muglin, and that the 33 kV line from Dhadingbesi to Ratomate is operating. It says it is working to restore supply across Nuwakot by 3pm Saturday.
Do not approach damaged power lines or try to reconnect a building yourself. Report hazards to local authorities or Nepal Electricity Authority staff.

posts.title: NDRRMA says 4,451 rescued, with 15,224 security personnel deployed
body: NDRRMA's 10am Saturday situation update says 4,451 people have been rescued in the flood response, the Kathmandu Post reports. The authority's earlier named nationality list totals 113, so it is not a full breakdown of the current total.

The same NDRRMA update says 15,224 security personnel are deployed for search, rescue and relief. That is a different count from figures published by the Prime Minister's Office and Home Administration on Friday, which used different reporting times and may cover different deployments.
Rescue work is continuing in the affected districts. Do not travel into the flood zone unless officials ask you to do so.

posts.title: Nepal tells foreign journalists covering the flood to get formal clearance
body: Nepal's Department of Information has told foreign journalists covering the Bhotekoshi flood to get formal clearance before reporting from the field, the Kathmandu Post reports.

Correspondents must submit their passport and visa, an appointment letter and recommendation from their own outlet, a recommendation from their country's foreign ministry or embassy in Nepal, an organisational identity card and details of their salary and benefits, then apply online and collect a press card in person with two passport sized photos.

Department spokesperson Govinda Prasad Pandey said the arrangement is not new and has long applied to foreign journalists under existing print and broadcast rules. An unnamed government official told the paper it is meant to streamline coverage of the disaster rather than set permanent policy.

posts.title: Armed Police Force says it has now sent over 4,800 personnel to the flood zone
body: The Armed Police Force said Saturday morning it has now mobilised more than 4,800 personnel for search and rescue, with base camps set up across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Tanahu, Gorkha, Chitwan and both Nawalparasi districts, Onlinekhabar reports.

That is well above the 1,845 Armed Police Force personnel the Home Administration named in Friday evening's tally of all security forces working the flood. It is not clear whether the two counts are measuring the same thing, and neither the Armed Police Force nor the Home Ministry has explained the gap.

posts.title: Nepal Telecom restores mobile service at 80 of 120 flood-hit sites
body: Nepal Telecom said Saturday it has restored mobile service at 80 of the 120 towers and sites knocked out by the flood in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading, The Rising Nepal reports. Technicians were flown in by helicopter to reach some of the most remote sites, including towers in Gosainkunda, Suryagadhi and Bidur municipalities. Service in Dhunche, the Rasuwa district headquarters, came back on Thursday.

Phone lines being down is the main reason families cannot reach relatives in the flood zone. If you are trying to find someone, keep trying the same number rather than assuming coverage in their area is still out.

posts.title: Damage put at Rs 200 billion, ADB approves $5m emergency grant
body: The Asian Development Bank has approved a US$5 million, about Rs 750 million, emergency grant for the flood response, the finance ministry said in an update reported by The Rising Nepal on Saturday. The Prime Minister's Disaster Relief Fund's balance has separately reached Rs 4.091 billion, up from Rs 2.172 billion before the latest round of deposits, which added Rs 1.918 billion between noon Wednesday and midnight Thursday. The fund had taken in Rs 273.3 million in its first six hours, led by a Rs 100 million gift from Gorkha Brewery. That is public donations, separate from the Rs 1 billion the government has already released for relief.
Physical Infrastructure Minister Sunil Lamsal said damage to roads and bridges is around Rs 200 billion. He called it preliminary information.

That figure does not include energy infrastructure. Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha has ordered an immediate assessment of hydropower damage. In Rasuwa, 8 projects have been hit, 5 of them operational with a combined 236 megawatts, and 3 still under construction with a combined 342 megawatts. Nuwakot has lost access to 6 more projects, 4 operational at 123 megawatts and 2 under construction at 53 megawatts.
Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan are still being surveyed for road and building damage, so the Rs 200 billion figure is expected to rise.

The government has released Rs 1 billion to the disaster relief fund, plus Rs 10 million each to Rasuwa and Nuwakot and Rs 5 million to Dhading. The World Bank has separately offered up to Rs 25 billion in emergency assistance, its Nepal country director told the finance ministry. That is aid, not a damage estimate.
Insurers say claims will take weeks to settle because most of the damaged sites cannot be reached by road.

UNICEF says at least 17,000 children have been affected across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. It counts 18 schools destroyed and 20 more damaged in those three districts, wider than the 8 schools Onlinekhabar had reported damaged in Rasuwa and Nuwakot alone a day earlier. UNICEF says around 10,000 school-age children now need help such as temporary classrooms and replacement books to keep learning.

posts.title: Australia's missing count rises to 41 after Friday evening dip to 38
body: Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade put the number of Australians unaccounted for in the flood at 41 by Saturday morning, ABC News reports, its highest count yet. DFAT said the number could still move as officials work through the list. Most of the missing Australians were on separate pilgrimages and tour groups heading for Mount Kailash.

The count has moved several times this week. Foreign Minister Penny Wong said Friday morning that 39 were unaccounted for, up from the 35 that Nepal's tourism board had listed a day earlier. DFAT said Friday evening that the count had eased to 38, after one of them, 26 year old Cara Severino, made contact with her family from Gosainkunda, saying she was walking toward Kathmandu with other hikers after being stranded at Kyanjin Gompa. It then rose again to 41 by Saturday.

Wong also announced A$5 million in Australian aid: 2 million to the World Food Programme, 2 million to Australian NGOs through the Australian Humanitarian Partnership, and 1 million to the Emergency Action Alliance for local recovery work. Three more Australian humanitarian specialists are being sent to join the 20 staff already in Nepal.

posts.title: European Union pledges 2 million euros in flood aid for Nepal
body: The European Union has allocated 2 million euros in humanitarian aid for Nepal's flood victims, the EU Delegation to Nepal said in a Friday statement reported by the Rising Nepal.

The money is meant to cover urgent needs including food, healthcare, clean water and sanitation. It comes on top of about 3 million euros the EU had already committed this year for disaster preparedness in Nepal.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Europe stands with Nepal as it responds to the flood.

posts.title: India's foreign ministry says 320 of its nationals still uncontactable
body: India's Ministry of External Affairs said Friday that 320 Indian nationals remain uncontactable in the flood, and that about 100 more people of Indian origin have also not been reached, ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, the Tribune reports. Jaiswal said the figures are still moving as officials work to reconcile several different lists of missing people.

About 400 Indian nationals stranded on the Chinese side of the border have been confirmed safe, with the Indian embassy in Beijing helping coordinate their evacuation, and 96 of them have already crossed into Nepal by land, the Tribune reports.
India has separately confirmed the rescue of 63 Indian workers from the Trishuli-1 hydropower project, and 21 Indians who reached Kathmandu from the flood zone have already gone on to Delhi.
This is India's own count of its nationals, kept by its own ministry. It is not the same figure as Nepal's missing list, and the two should not be added together.

posts.title: Two schools swept up in the flood, hundreds of students still being traced
body: More than 370 students were at Uttargaya Public School in Bidur Municipality, Nuwakot, when the flood hit on Wednesday morning. Vice principal Pawan Sharma told Onlinekhabar the school has only been able to contact around 40 percent of them so far, and that 25 to 30 percent have been handed over to their parents.

Sharma said the school no longer has records for the rest and is still trying to reach their families. Out of contact does not mean dead. Phone and internet lines are still down across much of the district.

At Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Nuwakot, principal Rajendra Dawadi and a group of 40 to 50 students and staff who fled to high ground were rescued on Friday, three days after the flood, Onlinekhabar reports. Dawadi said around 15 more students who also fled to higher ground are still waiting to be rescued, and two school employees remain out of contact.
Families looking for a student should go through the District Police Office or the local ward office, the same channels this page lists for anyone missing in the flood.

posts.title: Canada pledges $5 million as 32 Canadians remain unaccounted for
body: Canada's Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand said at a Friday briefing that 32 Canadians and permanent residents remain unaccounted for in the flood, up from 30 named a day earlier, the Canadian Press reports. Anand said the figures are likely to keep changing as officials work through the lists. No Canadians are among those confirmed dead, and none were among the 121 foreign nationals the Nepal Tourism Board said Friday had been rescued.

Global Affairs Canada has sent five consular officials to Kathmandu to support Canadians and work with local officials, and Anand said more could be deployed if needed. Secretary of State for International Development Randeep Sarai announced Canada is providing $5 million in humanitarian assistance, to be channelled through organisations such as the Red Cross. Global Affairs Canada says about 858 Canadians are registered as being in Nepal and 18 in the Tibet Autonomous Region.
Out of contact does not mean dead. Canadians with concerns about a family member in the flood zone should contact Global Affairs Canada's emergency watch and response centre.

posts.title: Prithvi Highway fully reopens after two days blocked by flood debris
body: The Prithvi Highway, the main road between Kathmandu and Pokhara, had been blocked since Wednesday evening after Bhotekoshi floodwater dumped mud across it in Gajuri and Galchhi, in Dhading, Onlinekhabar reports.

The Galchhi stretch reopened to alternating one way traffic on Friday evening, and the Galaundi, Ghatbesi and Jarekhet stretch reopened to two way traffic, Department of Roads engineer Rajiv Manandhar told the Kathmandu Post.

The whole highway reopened later on Friday evening once crews cleared the remaining mud and debris, the Kathmandu Valley Traffic Office said, Nepal News reports. Vehicles that had been stranded on the highway for days were being guided to safe locations overnight, and long distance public buses out of Kathmandu Valley were due to resume regular service from Saturday morning.
Officials have previously warned the road could shut again if heavy rain returns to the area.

posts.title: Researcher says an ice-rock fall off Langtang Lirung, not a lake burst, may have caused the flood
body: Santosh Nepal, a water resources and climate change researcher, told Onlinekhabar on Friday that the flood may have started with a huge ice and rock fall off Langtang Lirung rather than a glacial lake bursting, which was the earlier working theory.

He said satellite images show a mass of ice, snow and rock falling from about 5,000 to 5,500 metres on the mountain's northern slope and dropping nearly 2,000 metres into the Lhende Khola. The impact could have released enough energy to melt snow and ice fast enough to send a sudden surge of water downstream, without a lake first forming and bursting.

Nepal said the mechanism looks similar to Uttarakhand's 2021 Chamoli disaster, and that it is too early to conclude what happened. He said researchers still need more satellite data and a field investigation once conditions allow.
This is one researcher's preliminary reading, not a finding from the government or ICIMOD, and the cause of the flood is still not officially confirmed.

posts.title: Bharatpur Hospital runs out of freezer space as bodies near 200
body: Chitwan's hospitals are struggling to keep up with the bodies the flood has brought them. Bharatpur Hospital's freezers hold only 24 bodies, and most of that space was already taken by unclaimed bodies before the flood, chief medical superintendent Dr Bishwabandhu Bagale told Onlinekhabar. By Thursday evening 137 bodies had reached the hospital, and staff expected the total to reach around 200 by Friday evening.

Bodies that do not fit in the freezers have been kept in corridors and outside areas covered with tarpaulins, and some have started to decompose in the heat, Bagale said. Four forensic teams, reinforced by staff from Bheri Hospital, hospitals in the Lumbini region and Nepal Medical College, are working around the clock on post-mortems, fingerprints and photographs to identify the dead.

Identified bodies are being moved to a temporary, air-conditioned body management centre the government is setting up in a building near the Chitwan Industrial Association, on Vidhyut Road in Bharatpur. About 58 bodies had been processed and moved there by Friday afternoon, Onlinekhabar reports. Local business groups are supplying dry ice to slow decomposition while identification continues.
Chitwan has recorded more bodies than any other district in this flood, most of them carried down the Trishuli and Narayani from Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading.
Families looking for someone should go through the District Police Office or the local ward office rather than to hospitals directly, since those are the lists that get updated centrally.

posts.title: Trucking group says over 1,000 drivers, helpers and traders unaccounted for near the border
body: More than 400 container trucks are missing along the Rasuwagadhi-Kerung and Trishuli corridor, and the people who worked with them, drivers, helpers, labourers and traders, could number more than 1,000 out of contact, Arjun Bahadur Sapkota, president of the Nepal Truck Container Transportation Service, told Onlinekhabar.
This is the transport association's own count, not a figure from Nepal Police or NDRRMA, and it has not been confirmed by the government.

Sapkota said about 175 of the association's 966 registered trucks had gone toward Kerung just before the flood. He said customs delays at the Dhunche checkpoint had left 70 to 80 trucks parked along the highway for three or four days before they were swept away, and that 30 to 40 more were lost in Betrawati, Nuwakot.
Out of contact does not mean dead. Transport operators are asking the government to widen search and rescue to cover the drivers and workers along the route.

posts.title: Nepal's missing count nearly doubles to 1,924 as NDRRMA widens who it counts
body: Nepal's disaster authority NDRRMA said in a Friday evening Search, Rescue and Relief update that 1,924 people are now listed out of contact in Nepal, nearly double the 977 it had given that same afternoon. NDRRMA said the jump came from adding more local residents to the tally, not from a new wave of people going missing, AP reports. The count of foreign nationals held at 517, unchanged since Friday morning.

That evening update put NDRRMA's own separate figure for the dead at 579, and said more than 3,700 people had been rescued and about 14,800 security personnel were mobilised for the search, AP reports. Saturday's NDRRMA bulletin then listed 626 bodies, before Nepal Police's 4pm update reported 669. Nepal Police's earlier 6am figure was 616, before those later updates.

Separately, Province Police said 116 people from Madhesh Province remain out of contact, 10 fewer than earlier in the day after some reached their families, spokesperson SSP Prabhu Prasad Dhakal told Onlinekhabar.

Out of contact does not mean dead. Phone lines, power and internet are still down across large parts of the flood zone, and officials are still working through the lists as contact is slowly restored.
If you are trying to find someone in the flood zone, call the nearest District Police Office or 100, and register the same details with the local ward office.

posts.title: NDRRMA says 933 hydropower workers are among Nepal's missing
body: The Nepali Army has pulled more than 350 workers and local villagers out of a flooded access tunnel at the under construction Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, rescuers rappelling from a hovering helicopter to reach the entrance, Bloomberg reports, citing Nepal's Prime Minister's Office. More than 100 people were still believed trapped inside as of Thursday, and the operation is continuing.

The Nepali Army said separately that its units have rescued more than 300 people across the flood zone so far, spokesperson Brigadier General Raja Ram Basnet said, a wider tally than NDRRMA's earlier, named count of 113. It is not confirmed how these counts relate to each other. Around two dozen helicopters and nearly 1,000 personnel from the Nepal Police, Nepali Army and Armed Police Force are working the search, the Kathmandu Post reports.

At Trishuli 3A in Mailung, where 35 workers were reported cut off on Wednesday with the tunnel gate blocked, the army airlifted three people out on Thursday, Onlinekhabar reports. It has not said how many remain inside.

At the Langtang Hydropower project, more than 25 workers have been out of contact in a tunnel since Wednesday. Bijay Mohan Bhattarai, the company's managing director and a secretary of IPPAN, said government agencies need to step up rescue efforts there, and that all available helicopters had already been sent elsewhere, Onlinekhabar reports.

The Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation said Friday that a fresh landslide has completely buried the camp area of the Upper Trishuli-3B project in Nuwakot. It said rescuing people there is the top priority and that rescue equipment has been flown in, Onlinekhabar reports. It did not say how many people were on site.

The Independent Power Producers' Association Nepal, IPPAN, says 215 staff from five hydropower projects in total have not been reached since Wednesday's flood. Worst hit is Upper Trishuli-1 itself, with 94 people out of contact by IPPAN's count, a narrower figure than the more than 350 the army says it has now brought out of that project's tunnel. At Rasuwagadhi, 51 staff are out of contact, though 3 reached higher ground on their own.

Nepal's disaster authority NDRRMA said in its Friday evening update that 933 hydropower workers are among the 1,924 people it now lists as missing in Nepal, the Associated Press reports. That is a far bigger number than IPPAN's own count above, and NDRRMA has not broken its total down by project.

posts.title: Red Cross says at least 93,000 people affected by the flood
body: David Fisher, head of delegation for the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies in Nepal, said Friday that at least 93,000 people have been affected by the flood and are in great need, the Jerusalem Post reports.

It is the broadest estimate yet of how many people the flood has touched, wider than the confirmed death, missing and rescued counts on this page, and it has not been confirmed by the Nepali government.

posts.title: Government asks Meta and TikTok to remove flood misinformation and scam QR codes
body: Nepal's government has asked Meta and TikTok to remove graphic flood content, AI-generated videos and scam donation QR codes that have been circulating since the disaster, the Kathmandu Post reports.
Give only through the channels listed on this page, or the government's own portal at pmdrf.nchl.com.np. A donation QR code shared on social media is not verified unless it leads there.

posts.title: Rasuwa reconnected by a light-vehicle road, but still short of almost everything
body: Rasuwa was reconnected to the road network on Friday, when an alternative route reopened for small, four-wheeled vehicles between Kathmandu and Dhunche, via Tokha, Gadkhar Bridge, Narja, Lachyang, Saramthali and Kalikasthan, the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport said, Onlinekhabar reports. The flood had cut the district off after sweeping away 13 bridges inside Rasuwa and two more on the Nuwakot-Rasuwa border, destroying about 40 kilometres of road in total.

Conditions on the ground are still severe. About 3,500 people are sheltering in Uttargaya rural municipality alone, including students, displaced families, elderly people, pregnant women and people who need oxygen, local officials told Onlinekhabar.

Uttargaya chair Madhav Aryal said the municipality now has two ambulances and one vehicle left. "The minimum responsibility that the state should fulfil has not been met," he said. Gosainkunda chair Kaisang Nurpu Tamang described what supplies remain there in two words: "Nothing, nothing."

Around 150 people who fled a hydropower project are stranded across a river with no way to reach food, and 36 students are separated from their families in Nuwakot because access routes are damaged, Onlinekhabar reports.
Local officials in Uttargaya believe as many as 750 people from the municipality may still be missing. That figure is their own estimate and has not been confirmed by police or NDRRMA.

People trying to get aid into Rasuwa should coordinate through the district disaster relief committee or the army rather than travelling in on their own. The new route takes light vehicles only, and conditions can still change.

posts.title: Eighty Nepali truck drivers stranded in Kerung plead to come home
body: About 80 Nepali container truck drivers have been stranded for three days in Kerung, the Chinese border town across from Rasuwagadhi, since the flood wrecked the road home, the Kathmandu Post reports.
Rasuwa's chief district officer, Narendra Pariyar, said it is currently impossible to bring them back through the Rasuwagadhi border point because the road is destroyed.
Driver Krishna Bahadur Lamichhane told the paper 80 people have registered their names so far, and that they are paying for their own food and lodging in Kerung while they wait.

The Rasuwagadhi to Kerung road took the worst damage from the Bhotekoshi flood and is expected to stay impassable for months, so the drivers are asking officials to bring them home through an alternative border crossing instead.

posts.title: Nepal asks India and China to build 42 Bailey bridges in flood zone
body: Nepal has asked India and China for help building 42 Bailey bridges in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading, after most bridges there were destroyed by the flood and cut off two way road traffic, Onlinekhabar reports. NDRRMA assessed that number as urgently needed.
India's foreign ministry spokesperson said India would provide Nepal with assistance, including Bailey bridges, whenever required. No timeline for delivery has been given yet.

posts.title: Seven bodies believed to be flood victims recovered downstream in India
body: Authorities in India's Uttar Pradesh state have recovered seven bodies believed to have been swept downstream from Nepal's flood, district officials said Friday, AFP reports.

Four unidentified bodies were found in Maharajganj district on Thursday. "We think they have been swept into India from Nepal following flash floods there," district magistrate Gaurav Singh Sogarwal said. Three more bodies were recovered separately in Kushinagar district, about 70 kilometres further downstream.
None of the seven has been identified yet. They are not part of Nepal's own confirmed toll, since they were found across the border.

posts.title: Cabinet orders relief package, ministers to give a month's pay
body: Nepal's Cabinet made three flood relief decisions at its Thursday meeting, government spokesperson and Education Minister Sasmita Pokharel said on Friday, Onlinekhabar reports.
The Prime Minister and every member of the Council of Ministers will give one month's salary to the Prime Minister's Disaster Relief Fund.
The Cabinet approved Agriculture Inputs Company Limited to buy 25,000 tonnes of DAP fertiliser from India, government to government, to help farmers who lost supplies in the flood.

The Cabinet has told the Finance Ministry to prepare a relief and rehabilitation package for people and businesses affected by the flood in Rasuwa. The details of that package have not been published yet.

posts.title: Universities told to postpone exams from Friday because of the floods
body: Education and Sports Minister Sasmit Pokharel has directed university vice-chancellors to postpone all examinations scheduled from 29 August because of the floods, Onlinekhabar reports.
Universities are also told to suspend non-essential gatherings, workshops and seminars, and to arrange re-examinations for students who could not sit exams on 28 August.
The ministry said the order is meant to protect students, parents, teachers and staff while the disaster response continues.
